reference: Grand Seiko Heritage Collection Spring Drive 'Snowflake', ref. SBGA211 (the Grand Seiko-signed model; from memory it succeeded the Seiko-signed SBGA011 with the same case and dial texture). Chosen because the drawing shows exactly this layout: power-reserve indicator at 7-8, date at 3, blued centre seconds, dauphine hands and faceted batons with a broader marker at 12 on a white textured dial. Checked against the drawing's definition and kept. Finishes rest on two hands-on reviews that state them in words (Worn & Wound, Monochrome), on Grand Seiko's page, and on Worn & Wound's macro photographs.

surfaces.detail: A narrow, smoothly sloping bezel, Zaratsu mirror-polished (Worn & Wound: the lugs enwrap 'a polished bezel'). A thin bright step sits inside it against the crystal in Grand Seiko's product image.

Outside the bezel the only top surface is a band running from lug to lug on each side, hairline-brushed. Worn & Wound: 'Wide bands of brushing run across the entirety of the watch with a vertical grain, gently bowing out to be tangent to the bezel at three and nine'. At 3 and 9 the band pinches out, so the polished bezel meets the polished bevel there.
Wide flat lug tops with fine, even hairline brushing running lengthwise, continuous with the case top and matched by the bracelet.

'The brushing terminates in a perfectly sharp line, leading to a Zaratsu polished bevel that runs along the edge of the case of both sides' (Worn & Wound). The bevel is wide and flat and runs the whole length of each side, lug tip to lug tip.
Below the bevel the case tapers in toward the back, and Worn & Wound says 'This surface is also fully polished'. From the front it barely shows.

surfaces.direction: flutes parallel to the stem (9 to 3)
surfaces.detail: Deeply fluted screw-down crown at 3 with bright flutes, 'slightly recessed for protection' (Monochrome) rather than set behind guards. The polish is read from Grand Seiko's image.

surfaces.material: stamped metal blank, silver-plated under translucent coats
surfaces.detail: The white is not paint: Grand Seiko says the dial 'is not painted white but is made by a special silver-plating process'. It reads as a soft, faintly pearly matte white.

The 'Snowflake' pattern is a fine irregular relief like wind-crusted snow or handmade paper, stamped into the blank before plating (Monochrome). It has no repeat and no sunray; its short broken ridges run roughly 12 to 6 in both Grand Seiko's image and Worn & Wound's macro.

surfaces.direction: circular around the sub-dial's own centre
surfaces.detail: The power-reserve indicator at 7-8 is a fan-shaped window cut through the snow surface to a lower layer (Worn & Wound: 'visible on a sub-layer cut through the lovely snowy surface'). Its floor carries fine concentric grooves centred on the pointer's pivot. Along the outer arc runs a band of bolder radial flutes that narrows along its length, the 'slightly graduating scale', with a small black printed block at each end. There are no numerals.
Tall applied batons with a flat mirror top and bevelled mirror sides (Worn & Wound: 'flat mirrored surfaces on all sides'), slightly tapered; broader at 12 and none at 3.
A small applied polished emblem sits above the printed name under 12. The unbranded drawing leaves both off.
Small black minute blocks round the edge, with a bolder one beside the date, and a black gothic maker's name under 12. SPRING DRIVE is printed in dark blue above 6.
There is no luminous material anywhere on the hands or dial (Monochrome notes 'the absence of luminous material on the hands and dial').
Broad dauphine hands, diamond-cut. Worn & Wound: they are 'perfectly polished on top as well as on the razor-sharp bevels'. Each is a flat mirror top between two bevels, tapering to a sharp point.
A fine tapering blued-steel needle with a short broader tail (Grand Seiko: 'blue tempered steel seconds hand'). It glides continuously rather than ticking.
The power-reserve pointer is a short tapered polished hand on a round polished boss.

surfaces.material: blued steel hub with a bright pin
surfaces.detail: The seconds hand's round hub tops the stack and is blued like the hand, with a small bright dot at its centre (read from Grand Seiko's image and Worn & Wound's macro).
A raised rectangular frame at 3 with polished bevels (Worn & Wound: 'a square polished frame').
White with black numerals (Worn & Wound: 'a black on white date disk').
'Dual-curved sapphire crystal', gently domed, with 'Anti-reflective coating on inner surface' only (Grand Seiko).

surfaces.part: bracelet or strap at the lugs
surfaces.detail: Five-row bracelet: 'three brushed links alternating with two thin polished links' (Worn & Wound), with brushing that 'matches the lugs perfectly'.
No bezel insert or markings, no pushers, no screws, no crown guards.

lightBehaviour: The Zaratsu bezel and lug bevels behave as flat, undistorted mirrors: each plane turns white or black all at once as the lamp crosses its reflection angle, with hard edges.
The hairline lug tops and bracelet rows never mirror; they keep a soft linear sheen and stay mid-grey when the polished planes beside them go black.

The dial shows its texture only through tiny shadows: raking light from the side deepens the snow most, because the ridges run 12 to 6; frontal light flattens it to plain white, and it never goes glossy.
Each hand and marker facet is its own mirror, so a hand usually shows one bright and one dark plane that swap as the lamp or the hand moves, with a razor-sharp line between them.
The blued seconds hand swings from bright cobalt to almost black with angle; the power-reserve fan shows a small bow-tie sheen from its concentric grooves and a sparkle along its fluted rim.
geometry: Round case 41 mm across, 49 mm lug to lug and 12.5 mm thick. A narrow sloping bezel surrounds a gently domed sapphire. Broad lugs flow straight out of the case with no step, each with a flat brushed top and a wide flat polished bevel on its outer side; the brushed band narrows to nothing at 3 and 9, where the bezel touches the bevel. Crown at 3, half sunk into the flank, no guards. 20 mm bracelet.
avoid: Do not render the dial as white paint, lacquer or enamel, or give it a regular pattern or sunray: it is an irregular stamped relief under silver plating.
Do not stretch the snow texture sideways as the current sketch's noise does (it varies more slowly along 9-3): the real ridges run roughly 12 to 6.
No lume anywhere: hands and markers are solid polished metal.
Do not brush the bezel or polish the lug tops, and keep the line between hairline top and polished bevel sharp, never blended.
Do not draw the hands as flat two-tone triangles: they are multi-faceted mirrors. Only the seconds hand is blue.

The case is titanium (Grand Seiko's 'High-Intensity Titanium'), not steel. From memory titanium reads a touch greyer than steel, but the maker's images show it bright, so keep it close to a steel tone rather than dark grey.
The power reserve is a recessed fan with concentric grooves and a fluted rim, with no numerals, not a printed arc with ticks as in the current sketch.
From memory, the Seiko-signed predecessor SBGA011 has SEIKO at 12 with the GS emblem lower on the dial; the SBGA211 has the GS emblem and Grand Seiko at 12.
